reason: Bridge -> Reasoning: `given` took two independent counter-cases in one week. It claims "Fix cadence is automating while identifier assignment stays human-paced and request-driven". The 2026-07-28 bridge (validation.4c45723536f64ffc) records both of that day's vulnerabilities arriving fully labelled - CVE-2026-16812 at CVSS 10.0 with named fixed builds, a KEV entry and a three-day federal patch clock, and CVE-2026-53264 at CVSS 7.8 backported to seven stable lines - and the bridge itself flags the second as awkward, because a seven-branch backport is exactly the cadence the claim expects identifiers to fall behind, and identification kept up. The 2026-07-30 bridge (validation.a85bd5714ef4f884) is sharper still: Ruflo shipped a fix within 24 hours of disclosure carrying CVE-2026-59726, a CVSS 10.0 and a vendor-assigned name - fast fix and complete labelling on the same event. Reframe `given` away from "assignment cannot keep up" toward the narrower and still-supported mechanism the 07-30 bridge points at: Redis's own publication sequencing, plus unscored defaults (the unauthenticated MongoDB that bridge notes) that the identifier system never covers. `because` (the July 23 seven-branch release) stands as fact.
